newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Notorious Hong Kong gangster gets 30-year sentence.
newsitem.headline: Notorious Hong Kong gangster gets 30-year sentence.

text.p: One of Hong Kong's most notorious criminals, a jewellery thief and robber who spent seven years on the run after breaking out of jail in 1989, was sentenced to 30 years in prison on Monday.

Yip Kai Foon, 35 and paralysed from the waist down from a gun battle with police when he was captured last May, was found guilty last week of arms and explosive offences and firing at police to resist arrest.
The sentence on Monday by a High Court judge will begin only after he completes a previous 16-year jail term meted out to him in 1985 for arms and robbery offences.
A reputed master of disguise, Yip had spent only four years in prison when he escaped from a hospital toilet in 1989. He was believed to have fled to China.

From southern Guangdong province, he is believed to have forayed frequently across the border into wealthy Hong Kong where he was linked to a host of particularly violent armed robberies and jewellery heists.
Police found him by chance in central Hong Kong last year and a shootout ensued.
